content:
Earlier this year, the Liquid Glass design language made its debut on iOS, and now WhatsApp is exploring extending this design to more interface elements. Here are the details.

Liquid Glass is coming to WhatsApp's drawing editor and video player

If this sounds familiar, apologies for repeating it: WhatsApp is planning to expand the scope of its Liquid Glass redesign to more parts of the app.

Earlier this year, after more than six months of testing, WhatsApp finally rolled out its first wave of Liquid Glass updates more broadly.

At that time, WhatsApp was also working on applying the new design to elements like the voice message player, message reactions, and context menus, but these changes have been limited to the beta version of the app.

Now, according to WABetaInfo, the latest iOS beta version of WhatsApp shows that the company is preparing to bring Liquid Glass's visual style to more interface elements—namely, the progress bars in the drawing editor and video player.

Here's the content from WABetaInfo:

It's worth noting that some 9to5Mac readers have frequently reported that their iPhones still haven't received the first wave of Liquid Glass updates; however, today's news shows that Meta continues to adopt this new visual language, extending beyond iOS to include macOS and iPadOS.

Returning to today's news, WABetaInfo points out: "This feature is still in development and is not currently available to beta testers."
